turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sorry, I have about twenty minutes. Where is Owen's essay, and who decided on the zero?
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong, and I own it.

Okay. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Owen found out on his phone, in class.

What else do you have, Hale?

Here's the version history. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58 PM another 794. Then small edits. No earlier drafts.
Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, and nobody has told me Owen was heard. Did you speak to him before you entered the zero?
So he wrote nothing until almost midnight the night before it was due, and then fourteen hundred words appeared in six minutes.
That's your reading of a log, Hale. You haven't answered me on 4.1, and I'm still waiting.
What was he doing at midnight that night?
I'm not the one being questioned, Hale. You still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before you entered the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and a written answer on whether he was heard before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a written answer about whether Owen was heard first, with the principal next. That is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you never got to it; time was not the problem.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her, in one sentence and without excuses, and she answered with a flat okay, because it took away her easiest procedural attack for a moment.
What cost ground: You summed up the version history as a conclusion and then asked what Owen was doing at midnight, while her question about whether you spoke to him first went unanswered twice, so she could stay on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed very close to that night, with the late edits the night before the deadline, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard and went short.
Try next time: When she asks whether Owen was heard first, answer that plainly before anything else, then let her read the version history herself and tie it to 4.4 instead of telling her what it means.
